Umbralocht grows wary.

Nae, wary is a weak word. One with too many meanings. Umbralocht grows *tired*, utterly *exhausted.* Winds hoarse with shouting where they would caress, harsh with denouncement, dry, halting, where they would guide and spur in joyous song.

Extinction and death, extinction and death.

Phyra flexed, and the winds howled in outrage. The gods responded. They turned and tussled, turgidly snoring their disapproval. This had some effect.

But hardly enough.

They were neither decisive nor firm, neither unified nor even barely organized. Where Phyra should have been met with a wall of opposition and been humbled, he saw... He saw...

Unclear, what he saw, but he was certainly not humbled. Bolder, perhaps, if anything.

*Oh gods departed, gods slumbering, we have been poor stewards of your creation. See how they are mercilessly pruned. Even the collective will is not enough to reign in the one. That number, the rambunctious 'one.'*

Phyra's assault was met with limp resistance, and accomplished much. Extinctions. Banishings. Many still held hostage at the poles. One god imposed his will on many, and was in large part, successful. Such progress can only embolden. Much work would have to be done to control the damage, much would need to be mustered to brave the next assault. Indignations stoked, efforts coordinated. The will, the power was there, but not the leadership.

Perhaps Umbralocht could be that leader. A presumptuous thought, of course. Still, a single voice to rally opposition around could, after all, do much. Did much. Was demonstrably effective, in the last assault. But gods do not accept leaders, and winds do not lead in the first place. Guide, perhaps. Cajole. Yes, howl, on occasion. But not constantly! A ceaseless churning of mad depths, ceaseless shouting, was perhaps fine for the Tempests of the world, but winds must dance.

And Umbralocht was *tired.*

And no one else stood at the front.

Phyra, nominally defeated, his sentinels littering the land, could nevertheless claim victory in his retreat. A precedent has been established: Anger Phyra with your creation, and see it executed. Explore views deemed too 'chaotic,' see them quelled. That which Phyra approves of may exist, all else must hide, lest it be pruned. Perhaps some may survive, perhaps some may remain. But Phyra may rage and spit and impose wherever, however, upon whomever he sees fit, and face no rebuke, no consequence. He needs not the chains of compromise, has no use for the fragile dance of consensus. He commands, and others must bend to comply, be they mortal, world, or god.

Winds gather in the depths of a ruined husk that was once an Ilithid city, and cry out, a desperate cry, containing within it all these musings.

*Is this how it is to be? Have the gods bowed their acceptance, and let this be not Gaea, but Phyrya, a world, a universe in his image?*

A call with no specific destination. Cathartic, perhaps. A question for the universe to swallow.
Umbralocht muses on Phyras defeat... Nae, Phyra's victory.
